THE CANTONMENTS (ELECTIONS AND ELECTION PETITIONS) RULES, 1979
THE
CANTONMENTS (ELECTIONS AND ELECTION PETITIONS) RULES, 1979
S.R.O. 827(1)/79. (Gaz., Pak.,
Extra., Pt. II, 18.9.1979)---In exercise of the powers conferred by section
280 of the Cantonments Act, 1924, the Federal Government is pleased to make the
following rules, the same having been previously published as required by
sub-section (1) of that section, namely:--
PART I
INTRODUCTORY
AND GENERAL
1. Short title and commencement.---(1) These
rules may be called the Cantonments (Elections and Election Petitions) Rules,
1979.
(2) They shall come into force at
once.
2. Definitions.---In these rules, unless
there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,---
(a)
"Act" means the Cantonments Act, 1924 (II of 1924);
(b) "candidate" means a person proposed as candidate for, or
seeking election as, a member;
(c) "contesting candidate" means a validly nominated
candidate who has not withdrawn his candidature;
(d) "election" means election to a seat of a member held
under these rules;
(e) "election agent" means an election agent appointed by a candidate
under sub-rule (4) of rule 10;
(f) "electoral roll" means an electoral roll prepared under
rule 6;
(g) "member" means member of a Board;
(h) "nomination day" means the day specified under rule 8
for the nomination of candidates;
(i) "pollingv
agent" means a polling agent appointed under clause (a) of rule 24;
(j) "Polling
Officer" means a Polling Officer appointed under rule 23 for a polling
station.
((k) "President"
means the President of the Board or where a Board is not constituted, the
Officer Commanding the station;
(l) "Presiding
Officer" means a Presiding Officer appointed under rule 23 for a polling station;
(m) "returned
candidate" means a candidate who has been declared elected as a member
under these rules;
(n) "Returning
Officer" means a Returning Officer. Appointed under sub-rule (3) of rule 9;
(o) "scrutiny day" means the day specified under rule 8. for the scrutiny of nomination papers; .
(p) "validly nominated candidate" means a candidate whose nomination
has been accepted;
(q) "voter", in relati9n to a ward, means a person whose
name appears on the electoral roll for any electoral area in that ward; and
(r) "ward" means ward delimited under these rules.
3. Special provisions.---(1) If any
question arises as to the interpretation of these rules otherwise than in
connection with an election enquiry held thereunder,
the question shall be referred to the Federal Government whose decision shall
be final..
(2)
If any difficulty arises as to the
preparation of electoral rolls, delimitation
- of wards or conduct of elections, the Federal Government may by order do any thing not inconsistent with these rules
or with any provision of the. Act which appears to it to be
necessary for the proper preparation of rolls, delimitation of wards or conduct of elections. ,
(3)
When, under the provisions of any of
these rules, anything is required to be done on a specified day or
before the expiry of a specified period, and
that day or, as the ease may be, the last day of that period is a public
holiday within the meaning of section
25 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (XXVI of 1881), is to, be observed as a holiday in public offices in the cantonment, such thing shall be deemed to have
been done in time if it is done in the
cantonment on the next succeeding day which is neither a public holiday nor a day so observed.
4. Delimitation of cantonment into wards:---(1)
The Executive Officer shall prepare preliminary proposal' for
delimitation of wards and publish a copy thereof together with a notice
inviting; "objections and suggestions at his office or at such other place within the cantonment as he may consider
suitable.
(2)
The notice shall specify that objections or suggestions may be filed within such time as may be specified therein
and be presented to the Executive Officer.
